title: vpc-peering-egress-dns-tls-debug-scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad for the VPC peering / DNS / egress incident (customer X, private deployment in us-west-2). Mainly a stream-of-consciousness log of commands I ran, outputs, hypotheses, and TODOs. Use for postmortem input.

Background: customer spun up Private deployment in our VPC (rwi-private-usw2). They requested VPC peering from their VPC (cust-vpc-1234) to ours for control-plane and registry access. Peering was created ~2026-02-26. Symptoms reported: services in cust VPC cannot pull images from our internal registry, some API calls to control plane time out, occasional TLS errors from service logs.

Timeline and commands tried (local laptop, connected via dev bastion):

2026-02-27 09:12 - basic peering check
$ aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters Name=requester-vpc-info.vpc-id,Values=cust-vpc-1234
# output: PeeringState: active, AccepterVpcInfo: vpc-id=rwi-vpc-0a1b2c

2026-02-27 09:18 - route table verification (cust side)
$ aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=cust-vpc-1234
# found two route tables: main (no route for rwi CIDR), private-subnet-rt -> has route 10.10.0.0/16 -> pcx-0aaabbbb (peering).
# Note: some subnets still using main RT which lacked the peering route.

2026-02-27 09:45 - traceroute from cust instance to registry (internal.rwi.svc:443)
$ traceroute -n internal.rwi.svc 443
# hangs after first hop (local gateway), no path through peering.

2026-02-27 10:02 - DNS checks from cust instance
$ dig +short internal.rwi.svc A @10.0.0.2
# output: <empty>
$ nslookup internal.rwi.svc 10.0.0.2
# timeout after 5s

Hypothesis 1: DNS resolution for rwi private zone isn't set up for peered VPCs (Route 53 private hosted zone not associated or resolver rules missing).
What I tried:
- Verified private hosted zone (rwi.internal) exists in us-west-2 and is associated only with rwi-vpc-0a1b2c, not cust-vpc-1234.
- Checked for Route 53 Resolver rules: none configured to forward between VPCs.

Quick fix attempted (temporary): associate hosted zone with cust-vpc-1234 (requires approval). Did that for one subnet and retested DNS.
$ dig +short internal.rwi.svc @172.31.0.2
# now returns 10.20.3.12 (control-plane), progress!

But then new class of errors appeared: TLS handshake failures when service tried to pull images:
2026-02-27 11:33 - curl from cust instance:
$ curl -v https://internal.rwi.svc:443/v2/_catalog
* Connected to internal.rwi.svc (10.20.3.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* server certificate verification failed. CAfile: /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt CRLfile: none
* Unable to locally verify the issuer's authority.
curl: (60) SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches requested host name

Hypothesis 2: internal registry is presenting certs that don't include the peered DNS name (or we were resolving to an IP that maps to a different CN). Possible SNI mismatch or cert missing SAN for internal.rwi.svc. Also customer agents might be using IP to contact, which would fail cert name checks.

What I checked:
- On registry host, cert subject: CN=registry.internal.rwi.local, SANs: registry.internal.rwi.local, registry.rwi.svc (no internal.rwi.svc).
- Our DNS alias internal.rwi.svc points to load balancer that terminates TLS with a cert for internal.rwi.svc, but peered DNS was resolving to the control-plane IP (10.20.3.12) which has older cert.
- Looks like two different endpoints: registry LB (with correct cert) versus registry-backend instance (old cert). DNS resolution inconsistency depending on which VPC you're in.

Hypothesis 3: Egress/NAT/security-group rules on the peered side are blocking traffic to the registry LB or redirecting via a NAT with different IPs. Also potential asymmetric routing where traffic from cust-vpc to rwi vpc is allowed but return path blocked.

Commands to validate connectivity and SGs:
$ sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.20.3.12 and port 443 -w /tmp/pcap
# saw SYN from cust-instance, no SYN-ACK back (timing gaps).
$ aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-0c0d0e --query 'SecurityGroups[*].IpPermissions'
# rwi registry SG allows inbound 443 from rwi CIDR and from peering? It listed rwi/vpc-0a1b2c only. No explicit rule for cust-vpc-1234 CIDR.

Root cause (working theory combining evidence):
1) Private hosted zone not associated -> customer initially couldn't resolve internal names.
2) After associating, DNS resolved to an older backend instance IP because route53 record sets for internal.rwi.svc had an A record for both LB and a static internal IP used by the older host; VPC-local resolution favored that IP. That backend's cert didn't include the public internal.rwi.svc SAN -> TLS fails.
3) Security group / route asymmetry: traffic from cust-vpc traversing peering to backend hits SG that allows only rwi-vpc CIDR. Because peering doesn't translate source IPs, the backend sees cust source IP and drops it, so TCP handshake fails intermittently. This explains tcpdump seeing SYN with no SYN-ACK.

Immediate remediation performed:
- Associated Route 53 hosted zone with cust-vpc. (Temporary fix; we need org approval for long-term association.)
- Updated registry A records: removed stale A record pointing to old backend, forced LB-only DNS for internal.rwi.svc.
- Modified registry SG to allow inbound 443 from cust-vpc-1234 CIDR (restricted to the CIDR and limited to 443).
- Redeployed/rotated cert on the backend to include internal.rwi.svc SANs to prevent future mismatch (short-term, but still want LB fronting to be canonical).

Validation after fixes:
$ curl -v https://internal.rwi.svc:443/v2/_catalog
* Connected to internal.rwi.svc (10.20.100.21) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* Server certificate verified OK
< JSON list of repos >

$ docker pull internal.rwi.svc/myimage:latest
# success on first try from previously failing instance

Open questions / follow-ups (to include in postmortem):
- Why did Route 53 have both LB and direct backend A records? Owner of DNS records: platform-dns team (reach out to Priya). Was this a one-off leftover from migration?
- Long-term solution for DNS across peered VPCs: prefer Route 53 Resolver endpoints & rules or associate hosted zone? Pros/cons and security boundary. Document recommended pattern.
- Audit all SGs in rwi VPC for references to specific CIDRs vs. referencing Security Group IDs. Consider using SG-peering patterns or cross-account SG referencing where possible.
- Confirm whether peering primitives should enforce source IP preservation (they do), note in docs.
- Add automated checks for hosted-zone-to-vpc associations when onboarding private deployments.

Action items (owner -> due):
- Evan: write up quick remediation runbook (today) and link to PM/ops docs.
- Sana: contact platform-dns to clean up stale A records and confirm LB-only mapping (2026-03-05).
- Diego: review SG baseline for private deployment registries and propose least-privileged rule (2026-03-08).
- PM: decide on resolver vs hosted-zone association policy (by next sprint).

Notes to future self:
- When debugging peering issues, checklist: 1) route tables on both sides 2) security groups (ingress + egress) 3) NACLs 4) DNS resolution (private hosted zone associations vs resolver) 5) cert SANs and SNI 6) asymmetric routing / NAT behaviour.
- Keep tcpdump and curl outputs short in notes but grab full pcaps for SRE-runbook.

Raw error snippets saved to /var/tmp/private-deploy-incident-2026-02-27/ (on my laptop):
- curl error 60: SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches requested host name
- tcpdump: SYN only, no SYN-ACK (see pcap)
- traceroute: stops at peering-gateway hop

If we need to revert quick: remove hosted zone association for cust-vpc (if it's causing cross-tenant exposure), revert SG change, and switch customer back to using their NAT + internet egress to reach registry via public endpoint (if allowed). This is less ideal but safe rollback.

End of scratchpad. Will clean up and fold into incident postmortem.
